name: Australia

keyFacts.label: Popular Programs
keyFacts.value: VET Courses, General English, and Higher Education

overview.career: International students may work up to 24 hours per week during term — enough to practise your skills and build experience in the field you're studying, not just to earn. After graduating there are clear post-study work visa pathways in IT, engineering, health, and hospitality.
overview.culture: Multicultural and English-speaking, with a large and active Indonesian student community you can lean on in your first months. Halal food and places of worship are easy to find in the major cities, and most campuses run Indonesian student associations that organise regular gatherings.
overview.admission: Requirements vary by qualification level (VET, Bachelor, Master) — your counselor matches documents to the right pathway.
overview.livingCost: Varies by city — Melbourne and Sydney run higher than regional areas. See the monthly cost breakdown below.
overview.accommodation: On-campus dorms, homestays with a local family, and shared apartments are the three common options. We arrange this before you depart so you land with somewhere to stay, and help you weigh cost against commute — living further from campus is cheaper but adds daily travel.

whyStudy: Australia is the fourth most popular destination for international students — offering more than 1,200 schools with over 22,000 courses, high-ranked universities, and the chance to work while you study and after you graduate.

name: United Kingdom

overview.career: Graduate visa route allows post-study work; strong for finance, law, and research-focused fields.
overview.culture: Highly international student body, especially in London and Manchester.
overview.admission: Typically UCAS applications for undergraduate, direct university applications for postgraduate.
overview.livingCost: London runs highest; other cities like Manchester are more affordable. Ask your counselor for current estimates.
overview.accommodation: University halls of residence in year one, private shared housing after.

whyStudy: The UK offers shorter degree lengths (3-year Bachelor's, 1-year Master's), centuries-old institutions, and a Graduate visa route that lets students stay on to work after graduation.

name: United States

overview.career: OPT and STEM-OPT extensions offer 1–3 years of post-study practical training.
overview.culture: Extremely diverse, with strong international student services on most campuses.
overview.admission: SAT/ACT or test-optional for undergraduate; GRE/GMAT often required for graduate programs.
overview.livingCost: Wide range depending on state and city — your counselor can help compare options against your budget.
overview.accommodation: On-campus dorms are common in year one; off-campus housing after.

whyStudy: The US has the widest range of institutions and majors, flexible liberal-arts-style degrees, and Optional Practical Training (OPT) for hands-on work experience after study.

name: Canada

overview.career: Post-Graduation Work Permit length depends on program length; often a pathway to permanent residency.
overview.culture: Large, well-established Indonesian and broader international student communities.
overview.admission: Requirements vary by province and institution; college (diploma) and university (degree) pathways both available.
overview.livingCost: Toronto and Vancouver run higher than smaller cities — your counselor can help you compare.
overview.accommodation: Residence halls, homestays, and shared apartments near campus.

whyStudy: Canada is known for accessible tuition relative to the US/UK, a straightforward Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), and clear pathways toward permanent residency.

name: China

overview.career: Growing relevance for students pursuing business or trade careers connected to China.
overview.culture: Fast-growing international student population, with active scholarship programs.
overview.admission: HSK (Chinese proficiency) may be required for Mandarin-taught programs; not for English-taught tracks.
overview.livingCost: Generally lower than Australia, UK, US, or Canada — details vary by city.
overview.accommodation: On-campus dormitories are standard and typically the most affordable option.

whyStudy: China offers a growing number of English-taught programs, government and university scholarships, and strong options for students pairing Mandarin study with their degree.

name: Japan

overview.career: Strong demand for Japanese-language-proficient graduates in manufacturing, IT, and tourism.
overview.culture: Structured, safety-focused environment with a well-established international student support system.
overview.admission: Language schools typically require JLPT N5 or above; degree programs vary by institution.
overview.livingCost: Tokyo runs higher than Osaka and other regional cities — ask your counselor for current figures.
overview.accommodation: Dormitories and share houses are common for international students.

whyStudy: Japan pairs respected universities and language schools with JLPT-linked pathways, making it a strong fit for students combining language study with a degree or career move.

featuredPrograms.name: Language School
featuredPrograms.description: JLPT-aligned Japanese language pathways ahead of university or work.
